scope: Static review of unapproved proposals; no experiment results or hypothesis transitions

findings.title: Even challenge kernels and invalid random-RHS null
findings.correction: For an even-weight challenge in the degree-n negacyclic ring modulo 2^b (the draft uses power-of-two n), the nonzero vector with every coefficient 2^(b-1) is in its multiplication kernel. Multiple even-weight challenges retain that common ambiguity on the unrestricted coefficient domain; a bounded-secret uniqueness result needs a separate argument. For power-of-two n, an odd-weight challenge is a unit modulo 2 and hence modulo 2^b; more generally this part of the argument requires explicit invertibility. For an invertible challenge every RHS is consistent, so random RHS is not an inconsistency control.

findings.title: Condition collision costs on actual accepted-mask equality
findings.correction: A capped attack does not establish infinite recovery cost. Distinct random messages are not guaranteed unique; repeated message and randomizer may intentionally repeat deterministic masks. Missing-key-prefix work must charge accepted-counter search. Under independent usable-pair probability p_same and an h-bit randomizer, the pair approximation is N(N-1)*p_same/2^(h+1), giving birthday scale proportional to sqrt(2^h/p_same), not sqrt(2^h)/p_same. The conditional p_same model must be derived or measured under the actual acceptance process.

findings.title: Sign bytes do not bound the entire challenge image
findings.correction: FIPS 204 Algorithm 29 consumes the first eight bytes for signs and subsequent bytes for positions. Truncating only sign bytes leaves C(256,39) possible supports, whose base-2 logarithm is about 153.7603. A 16-to-32-bit full-image claim requires a different, fully specified seed truncation map. Uniform seed sampling does not imply uniform challenge-image sampling; exact forgery probability requires the induced distribution.

findings.title: Fresh shares retain joint dependence on the secret
findings.correction: Re-randomizing shares preserves their combined secret even when each individual share is uniform. It is not a secret-independent higher-order null. Define a null with independently generated secrets or a specified joint leakage law and verify the claimed independence.

findings.title: Rounded public keys and zero-matrix non-identifiability
findings.correction: ML-DSA publishes rho and t1 after Power2Round with d=13, not the full t. Zero A slots therefore do not directly reveal exact s2 slots from the stated public key. At A=0 the public key is independent of s1, so original-secret recovery by linear algebra is impossible without additional information. Distinguish original-secret identification, equivalent signing capability, and partial information; specify the actual public observation before building hints.

findings.title: One faulty transcript gives a fixed-target match
findings.correction: Matching one fixed h-bit randomizer among N independent honest transcripts has probability 1-(1-2^-h)^N. Its constant-success scale is 2^h, not 2^(h/2). Birthday or two-set collision costs require multiple variable targets and an explicitly charged pair model.

findings.title: Removing one rejection condition does not remove all gates
findings.correction: A narrower mask can eliminate the z-bound rejection only under its explicit parameter inequality. Low-bit, c*t0 and hint-weight rejection checks remain. Record and analyze each gate and the final accepted-signature law; do not assume every attempt is accepted.

findings.title: Structured covert payloads can be publicly distinguishable
findings.correction: A fixed all-zero k-bit payload forces a public challenge prefix that occurs with probability 2^-k under the honest model. Secret-key knowledge is unnecessary for this distinguisher. Any indistinguishability claim needs an explicit randomized/encrypted payload distribution, receiver protocol, and stated adversarial scope; bounded tests are not a universal proof.

findings.title: Recompute the CRT structure at each ring degree
findings.correction: Complete linear splitting of x^n+1 over F_q requires 2n dividing q-1 in the stated power-of-two cases. Thus n=256,q=257 does not provide 256 base-field slots. Conversely n=64,q=3329 is fully split into 64 linear factors, not 32 quadratic factors copied from n=256. Freeze a valid per-cell CRT map. Entry 49 also needs a separate exact-constraint path for zero hint noise instead of division by a zero standard deviation.

findings.title: Orbit controls must remain in the actual attack lattice
findings.correction: Rotation invariance of a homogeneous module lattice does not establish invariance of a target embedding or its projected block. A coordinate-permuted vector explicitly outside the lattice cannot be inserted as an ordinary sieve control. Specify the exact lattice and projection, certify membership of every injected vector, and test rejected nonmembers separately from valid algorithm comparisons.

findings.title: Repeated noisy alarms need not multiply the entire search cost
findings.correction: Under the proposed model of deterministic true failure, independent false alarms of probability epsilon, and at most k extra queries per first alarm, the expected query multiplier over F/p base candidates is at most 1+k*(p+(1-p)*epsilon). At p=2^-14, epsilon=0.01, k=6 this is about 1.06036, while the false-confirmed/true ratio is at most (1-p)*epsilon^(k+1)/p. This valid confirmation strategy contradicts the proposed universal hundred-fold lower bound. It is a conditional accounting counterexample, not a measured end-to-end attack cost.

findings.title: Parallel efficiency acts on work, not linearly on an exponent
findings.correction: For serial work T=2^a, t workers and efficiency E, elapsed work units are T/(tE), with logarithm a-log2(t)-log2(E). Aggregate processor work is T/E. Dividing the exponent a by E is not either quantity. Define elapsed, aggregate, and memory units separately.

findings.title: CBD(2) moments and matched-variance controls
findings.correction: CBD(2) has variance 1, fourth moment 5/2, and excess kurtosis -1/2. Uniform integers from -2 through 2 have variance 2. A matched-variance uniform or discrete-Gaussian control needs an explicitly normalized integer law and its actual moments, rather than reusing unmatched labels or assuming the Gaussian parameter equals realized variance.

findings.title: A finite log-lattice computation is not automatically exact CVP
findings.correction: There is no uniform probability distribution on an unbounded real span. Specify a bounded sampling window or quotient domain. A 200-bit numerical log basis and integer enumeration need certified approximation-error bounds and a comparison margin before they establish exact CVP in the real log lattice. Otherwise label the outcome numerical and keep theorem-domain and exactness questions unresolved.

findings.title: Planted-relative norms do not certify approximation factors
findings.correction: Because lambda_1 is at most the planted vector norm, output_norm/planted_norm is a lower bound on output_norm/lambda_1, not a certified upper approximation factor. Report the planted-relative ratio separately or supply a certified lower bound on lambda_1. A claim at dimension 256 also requires a theorem actually covering the tested lower dimensions before those cases can falsify it.

findings.title: Module and embedding dimensions need a valid cell map
findings.correction: Dimensions 50 and 70 with module rank 4 do not give integer ring degrees. Specify admissible ring degree/rank and the resulting embedding dimension per cell before execution; do not silently round or drop cells.

findings.title: The stated dense quantum-state cell exceeds the memory contract
findings.correction: The n=8,q=17 complex128 state alone needs 17^8*16 = 111612119056 bytes, exceeding the 32-GiB memory bound before temporary arrays. The claim that every cell is at most 41^4 amplitudes is false. Resolve the cell/memory contradiction prospectively; a sparse or compressed algorithm requires its own representation and fidelity contract.

findings.title: Average and worst-case quantifiers do not supply a numerical radius
findings.correction: An average-case versus worst-case distinction alone proves no quantitative radius separation. Small-dimensional numerical oracle tests cannot establish a general worst-case impossibility theorem. State the actual modeled threshold and retain the missing reduction or bound as an obligation.

findings.title: Use the correct time-memory slope direction
findings.correction: For slope s=d(log T)/d(log M), the derivative of log(M*T) is 1+s. A prediction s<=-2 contradicts wording that requires s>=-2. Reconcile the direction and limit conclusions to the prespecified interval; a finite interval does not bound all possible memory regimes.

findings.title: WOTS checksum antichain and minimum reachable chain index
findings.correction: For base-w message digits b, checksum C=sum(w-1-b_i). If a different b' dominates b componentwise then C'<C, so the full message-plus-checksum encoding cannot also dominate componentwise. The full encoding is an antichain. Identical encodings caused by a message-digest collision are a separate case. For several disclosed chain values, the minimum index per chain determines forward reachability, not the maximum. Entry 83 also uses h=8,d=3 with nonintegral layer height and d=2 makes layer 0 and layer d-2 identical; its comparison grid needs correction.

findings.title: Address headroom and reachable-domain coverage
findings.correction: Repeated use of the same logical ADRS is not an encoding collision: exhibit distinct logical addresses with identical encoded bytes. Key generation builds the top XMSS root; a finite signature sample does not enumerate every reachable tree address. FIPS 205 Table 2 gives bottom-tree widths 63 bits for 128f and 64 bits for 256f in the 8-byte field, so their headrooms are 1 and 0 bits rather than at least 8. Zero headroom within the field capacity does not itself imply a vulnerability. Freeze the reachable-domain enumeration and validate any claimed cross-type collision on the complete retained type byte.

findings.title: One million trials cannot resolve a 64-bit collision probability
findings.correction: Outputs of 8 and 12 bytes mean 64 and 96 bits. One million independent attempts at probability 2^-64 have expected hits about 5.42e-14. Zero hits cannot estimate that probability within a factor of two or support a collision-slope fit; its one-sided 95% binomial upper bound is about 2.996e-6. Report the bounded mutation coverage and a valid interval. Changing output truncation would require an explicitly revised prospective protocol.

findings.title: Shared public seeds do not erase hash address domains
findings.correction: The full function domain includes the public seed, address type, chain and index, and hash role. Sharing a public seed alone does not place all chain values into one common target function. Partition targets by the complete tweak domain and independently verify candidate relations under the actual function before using a multi-target cost model.

findings.title: Interior skips differ from valid chain-prefix truncation
findings.correction: If an interior iteration is skipped while the address counter advances, the next hash uses a different domain; the result need not equal a valid earlier chain value. A prefix-truncation fault is a different model. Specify fault position and counter behavior and verify the resulting chain index before applying the lower-index recovery argument.

findings.title: The stated second-preimage ratio has the wrong threshold
findings.correction: Under the draft's own expressions the MD/sponge ratio is 2^(c-n)/blocks. At c=32,n=24 and blocks=64 it is 4, not at most 1/16; at blocks=8 it is 32. The crossover is n>c-log2(blocks), not n>c/2. Charge expandable-message preparation and compare the best available generic direct attack. Truncated SHAKE is not itself the block-cipher permutation required for a Davies-Meyer construction; define the concrete compression function.

findings.title: Cache detection needs valid dimensions and trusted initialization
findings.correction: h=9,d=4 has nonintegral layer height. The top-L cache size is a geometric sum and is zero at L=0, unlike the stated largest-term expression. Detection also needs trusted cache initialization and defined misses; storing the first faulty value cannot detect that first use. Freeze valid cells and the trusted-cache fault model.

findings.title: A proof upper bound is not an exact attack frequency
findings.correction: Security-proof upper-bound terms are not exact conditional probabilities for an arbitrary selected forger. A measured frequency below a bound does not justify deleting the bound term. Define the reduction/extraction event and its inequality direction before interpreting the empirical comparison.

findings.title: Changing an exact weight can destroy importance-sampling support
findings.correction: A nominal law supported on exact weight w and a proposal supported only on higher exact weights are disjoint. Then the nominal measure is not absolutely continuous with respect to the proposal, and likelihood-ratio importance sampling cannot estimate the nominal expectation. Require positive proposal mass everywhere on nominal support, exact normalized P/Q weights, a justified range or tail bound, and separate pilot/evaluation data before claiming finite confidence intervals.

findings.title: Permuting whole key labels preserves a DFR-tail statistic
findings.correction: Relabeling whole keys leaves the multiset of per-key failure rates and its p99/median ratio unchanged. It is not a null for key-dependent heterogeneity. Specify a valid outcome-level exchangeability or conditional null and retain dependence on the corrected importance-sampling support contract.

findings.title: ISD algorithm and preprocessing grids omit named comparisons
findings.correction: The variable ledger lists Stern and MMT but the claim includes Dumer; its 2^10 and 2^18 levels omit the 2^14 A/A cell. An eight-bit gap does not resolve a crossover within one doubling without a specified interpolation model. Reconcile the algorithm set, A/A cell and comparison resolution before approval.

findings.title: The circuit-depth comparison names an absent cell
findings.correction: C2 requires depth 2^64 while the independent levels list only 2^40 and 2^96. Reconcile the prospective comparison and full cell map before approval.

findings.title: Calibration verdict and algorithm scope disagree
findings.correction: The contract lists Stern and BJMM while its claim covers Prange, Stern, Dumer and BJMM. A negative offset exceeding five bits cannot be described as calibration within three bits. Reconcile the algorithm scope and positive/negative decision text before approval.
